title: TUA & Synthe Brings Futuristic Cocktails and Pan-Asian Cuisine to Kolkata
excerpt: A new drink-and-dine destination pairs Chef Vaibhav Bhargava's Pan-Asian menu with Ankur Chawla's decade-themed cocktail programme spanning 2030 to 2110.
body:
• TUA & Synthe has opened in Kolkata with a Pan-Asian menu curated by Chef Vaibhav Bhargava, featuring dishes like Miso Salmon and Japanese Cold Avocado Pizza
  • The cocktail programme, developed by Ankur Chawla, draws inspiration from future decades between 2030 and 2110, with each drink designed to represent a different era's cultural influences
  • The restaurant positions itself as both a dining and nightlife destination, expanding Kolkata's growing premium Pan-Asian food scene

Kolkata has a new contender in its rapidly expanding upscale dining scene. TUA & Synthe, a drink-and-dine concept centred on Pan-Asian cuisine and inventive mixology, has opened its doors in the city, according to BW Hotelier. The restaurant merges two distinct experiences under one roof — a curated food menu spanning multiple Asian culinary traditions, and a beverage programme built around an unusual futuristic theme.

The Menu: Pan-Asian With Range

Chef Vaibhav Bhargava has put together a menu that draws from Japanese, Chinese, Korean, and Southeast Asian traditions without confining itself to any single one. Standout dishes include Miso Salmon, Japanese Cold Avocado Pizza, King Oyster Mushrooms in yuzu gochujang sauce, Grilled Teriyaki Salmon, and Hazelnut Kung Pao Chicken. The menu also features a selection of small plates, larger mains, and Asian-inspired bar bites designed for sharing over drinks.

The range signals ambition. A yuzu gochujang sauce on king oyster mushrooms nods to Korean flavours, while the cold avocado pizza borrows from Japan's knack for reimagining Western dishes. The Hazelnut Kung Pao Chicken, meanwhile, puts a textural twist on the Sichuan classic by substituting the traditional peanuts with hazelnuts.

Cocktails From the Future

The beverage side may be the more talked-about half of the concept. Ankur Chawla has built a cocktail programme structured around a series of drinks, each inspired by a future decade between 2030 and 2110. The idea is that every cocktail represents the flavours, themes, and cultural influences of a particular era yet to come.

"Each cocktail is designed to represent the flavours, themes and cultural influences of a particular era."

— TUA & Synthe's concept statement, via BW Hotelier

Signature cocktails carry names that match the playful concept: Appetite for More, Been There Done That, Controlled Chaos, Tough to be Simple, and Cherry on the Top. The names alone suggest a bar that prizes personality and storytelling as much as technique.

Kolkata's Pan-Asian Moment

TUA & Synthe arrives at a time when Kolkata's dining landscape is leaning increasingly toward Pan-Asian cuisine. The city — with its deep historical ties to Chinese food through the Tangra Chinatown neighbourhood — has long had an appetite for Asian flavours. Restaurants like Chowman, Ping's Cafe Orient, and Peter Hu have built loyal followings, while newer entrants continue to push the category upmarket. TUA & Synthe's combination of a serious kitchen and a concept-driven bar positions it as both a dinner destination and a late-night option.

Why It Matters for the Diaspora

For Indians abroad, Kolkata's food scene has historically been synonymous with Bengali classics — fish curries, mishti doi, rosogolla. The emergence of restaurants like TUA & Synthe reflects a broader shift in Indian metros, where globally influenced dining concepts are becoming mainstream. Visitors returning home will find a city whose restaurant culture increasingly mirrors the fusion-forward, cocktail-forward dining they encounter in cities like London, Singapore, or New York. Kolkata, it turns out, is no longer just about the neighbourhood Chinese joint — though those remain essential, too.

What's Next

TUA & Synthe has not yet disclosed pricing details or reservation policies. Diners interested in the concept can expect a premium positioning, given the calibre of the culinary and mixology teams involved. Whether the futuristic cocktail theme proves a lasting draw or a novelty will depend on execution — but the Pan-Asian menu, with its range from bar bites to full mains, gives the restaurant a solid foundation to build on.
